So the ice crowned Mako today. Ice crowns melt by noon, little friend.
I heard the final whistle from my boat. Sounded like a gull laughing.
She won, hm. A fast paw and a slow hook, and the puck goes where it wants.
Mako's stick knows the way. Yours will learn it, one winter at a time.
A lost game is a knot in the line. You can untie it or cut it. Untie it.
She beat you? Good. Now you know how fast fast can be.
The rink is a pond. The puck is a minnow. Mako is a hungry heron.
I saw her glide past the bakery, tail high as a mast. Let her sail.
Your paws were steady. Hers were quicker. The ice chose quicker today.
Do not measure yourself against Mako. Measure against yesterday's you.
Mako bragged to the whole dock. The crabs didn't clap. I didn't either.
A champion is just a cat who fell and got up one more time. You'll get up.
Her victory is a bright fish. It will spoil if she carries it too long.
You lost by a whisker. Whiskers grow. Skill grows slower, but it grows.
The tide brought her a win. The tide brings everyone something. Wait yours.
I told her well played. She grinned so wide I saw yesterday's dinner.
Mako skates like a cat who forgot to be careful. That is a gift and a risk.
One game is one cast. The lake is full of casts, little friend.
She won, and you watched. Watching is half of learning, hm.
The ice remembers every paw. Today it remembers hers. Tomorrow it forgets.
Do not sulk on my dock. Sulking scares the fish. Sit and watch the water.
Mako's bragging is like a bell on a buoy. You always hear it coming.
A quick loss is better than a slow victory. You learn faster, hm.
She beat you fair. Fair is the only kind of beating worth respecting.
The score is a number. The sore paws are a lesson. Keep the lesson.
I have lost to quicker cats. I just baited my hook and fished on.
So Mako is the champion of paw hockey. The harbor is champion of patience.
Let her strut. Strutting is good for the legs. Yours will need them next time.
You played with heart. Heart is not a score. Heart is a tide that returns.
Mako won today. The sun wins every morning, and nobody brags for it.
She skated like a swallow. You skated like a cat thinking. Both fly, in their way.
The ice was fast. She was faster. Next time, be the ice.
I hear she scored the last goal with her eyes closed. Or so she says, heh.
A loss is a stone. Keep it in your pocket. It will steady your stance.
Do not chase her record. Chase the puck. It is slower and more honest.
Mako's victory is a fresh fish. It will not keep. Yours will be smoked and stored.
You lost a game. Not a season. The season is long as a river.
She beat you, and now she floats like a cork. Corks float. They also drift.
Old cats like me win by not playing. That is a secret. Keep it, hm.
The rink taught you where the ice is soft. That is worth more than a medal.
Mako crowed so loud my bait jumped. I put it back. Fish don't care for hockey.
Her stick was quick. Your heart was steady. Steady lasts longer than quick.
One match is one tide. The sea has many tides, little friend.
I am quietly proud of you both. Do not tell Mako I said that, hm.
She won, and you lost, and the harbor still smells of salt and fish. All is well.
Mako's bragging is weather. It passes. Bring a hat and wait it out.
The ice does not apologize for being slippery. You learn to grip.
You will beat her next time, or you will not. Either way, we fish tomorrow.
A good opponent is a gift. Mako gave you a gift. It stung. Gifts do that.
She passed my boat shouting her score. I chuckled into my tea. The tea was good.
Mako's left paw is the tricky one. The right just makes noise, heh.
The pond does not mock the leaf that falls. It carries it. Let it carry you.
Every champion was once the cat who lost and kept playing. You are that cat.
She beat you fair, and now she puffs like a pufferfish. Let her puff.
The score was close as two fish in a net. Close is not a loss. Close is a promise.
Do not worry, little friend. The tide owes you one. I have seen it pay.
Mako skates like a herring dodging a net. You skate like a cat who knows the net.
The ice remembers every paw. Today it remembers hers. Tomorrow, who knows.
You learned more in one loss than she did in one win. That is the fisher's truth.
So she won. Good. Now the ice has a champion and you have a reason.
